title: Sections of a universally nonnegative perfect complex form an affine space of finite presentation
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Quasi-coherent modules are as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and ordinary tensor pullback and direct image are [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived pullback uses K-flat resolutions with flat terms and derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. A perfect object is etale locally isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$, and let $K\in D(\mathcal O_B)$ be perfect. For each scheme morphism $g:T\to B$, assume $\mathcal H^i(Lg^*K)=0$ for every $i<0$, where cohomology sheaves are kernels modulo images of a representing complex. Define $H^0(T,Lg^*K)=H^0(R\Gamma(T,Lg^*K))$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. The functor on schemes over $B$ given by $g\mapsto H^0(T,Lg^*K)$, with transitions induced by derived pullback and its composition isomorphisms, is represented by an algebraic space $V\to B$, naturally in every scheme test. Moreover $V\to B$ is affine and of finite presentation: its base change to every affine scheme over $B$ is an affine scheme, and it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $B$ or its test schemes is imposed.

proof.text: Put $F(T,g)=H^0(T,Lg^*K)$. This is an etale sheaf on scheme tests over $B$: fix $g:T\to B$. The connective-sections lemma identifies its values after any etale $h:T'\to T$ with sections of $\mathcal H^0(Lg^*K)|_{T'}$. Indeed etale tensor pullback is localized restriction; restriction is exact, so it computes derived pullback and commutes with kernels, images and cohomology. The lemma identifies the transition maps with those restrictions. Matching sections therefore glue uniquely by the module-sheaf axiom. This applies to every test $T$, including nonaffine and empty tests.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: first sentence and sheaf argument

proof.text:
Apply the local-model lemma to obtain an affine etale cover $u_\alpha:U_\alpha\to B$ and bounded finite free complexes $P_\alpha^\bullet$ in nonnegative degrees. Each is K-flat by the bounded-above-flat theorem. Consequently, for every scheme map $h:T\to U_\alpha$, the pullback complex $h^*P_\alpha^\bullet$ represents $L(u_\alpha h)^*K$, with the canonical derived-pullback composition isomorphism. It is still zero below degree zero. The connective-sections lemma now gives, naturally in $h$,
$$F(T,u_\alpha h)=\ker\bigl(\Gamma(T,h^*P_\alpha^0)\to\Gamma(T,h^*P_\alpha^1)\bigr).$$

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: finite locally free truncation and K-flat pullback

proof.text:
Fix a chart $U_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}A$, write $P^0=\mathcal O^n$, $P^1=\mathcal O^m$ (rank zero if absent), and let $d^0$ have matrix $(a_{ji})_{1\leq j\leq m,1\leq i\leq n}$. Define
$$C_\alpha=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(\sum_{i=1}^n a_{ji}x_i\mid1\leq j\leq m),\qquad V_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}C_\alpha.$$
For arbitrary $h:T\to U_\alpha$, the affine-target morphism bijection identifies maps $T\to V_\alpha$ over $U_\alpha$ with $A$-algebra maps $C_\alpha\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Sending $x_i$ to $f_i$ is exactly a tuple satisfying $\sum_i h^\sharp(a_{ji})f_i=0$ for every $j$, which is the preceding kernel. The inverse sends such a tuple to polynomial evaluation and factors through the quotient since each displayed relation evaluates to zero. Thus $h_{V_\alpha/U_\alpha}\simeq F|_{U_\alpha}$, naturally on all tests. Pullback sends each $f_i$ to its pulled-back section, which verifies naturality explicitly. The displayed finite algebra presentation gives local finite presentation of $V_\alpha\to U_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: matrix and polynomial quotient construction

proof.text: On $U_{\alpha\beta}=U_\alpha\times_B U_\beta$, the two pullbacks of $V_\alpha,V_\beta$ represent the same restricted functor $F$, hence Yoneda supplies the unique isomorphism identifying their section bijections. On triple overlaps their two composites induce the same transformation of $F$, so faithfulness gives the cocycle, and likewise the identity on diagonal overlaps. Under the relative-Spec anti-equivalence these become isomorphisms of the quasi-coherent coordinate algebras, compatible with arbitrary base change. The jointly surjective etale family $\{U_\alpha\to B\}$ is an fppf covering by the covering calculus, so quasi-coherent descent applies to their underlying modules. The descended sheaf has a commutative algebra structure: for sections on any small etale test, restrict to the covering tests, multiply (or take the unit) there, and glue by the sheaf axiom. The overlap algebra maps preserve these operations, so the products match; uniqueness of gluing proves all ring identities and scalar compatibility. Thus a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A$ on $B$ is obtained whose pullbacks are the coordinate algebras of the $V_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: etale descent, implemented on coordinate algebras

proof.text: Set $V=\operatorname{Spec}_B(\mathcal A)$ by the relative-Spec correspondence. It is an algebraic space affine over $B$, and $V\times_B U_\alpha\simeq V_\alpha$. For each scheme test $T\to B$, the schemes $T\times_B U_\alpha$ etale-cover $T$. On them the local bijections of step 3 agree on overlaps by their construction in step 4. Both $\operatorname{Mor}_B(-,V)$ and $F$ are etale sheaves, so these bijections glue: a matching tuple of local sections on either side gives a unique global section on that side. The two glued maps are inverse because their restrictions are inverse. For a map of arbitrary tests, restrict this assertion to the induced etale covers; local naturality from step 3 and uniqueness of gluing give global naturality.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: descent of local section representations

proof.text: The chart morphisms $V_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ are locally of finite presentation by step 3, so the chart criterion makes $V\to B$ locally of finite presentation. The affine-locality theorem makes it quasi-compact and separated. For any scheme test $T\to B$, it also says $V_T$ is a scheme and $V_T\to T$ is affine, hence separated; the scheme separated-implies-quasi-separated lemma makes its relative diagonal quasi-compact. Thus the diagonal of $V\to B$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Together these say that $V\to B$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation, hence of finite presentation. Affineness also gives affine scheme source after every affine scheme base change. No Noetherian assumption or global degree bound was used.
